Appendix C Electron form factor for DM scattering off electrons in a crystals

In crystals, a DM particle excites an electron from a Bloch state |n​k→⟩|{n\vec{k}}\rangle to another Bloch state |n′​k→′⟩|{n^{\prime}\vec{k}^{\prime}}\rangle, where nn and n′n^{\prime} are the band index labels in the first Brillouin Zone (BZ). Thus, the form factor |fi→f​(q→)||f_{i\to f}(\vec{q})| in Eq. (64) is

|fi→f​(q→)|2=|fn​k→→n′​k→′​(q→)|2=|∫d3​x​ψn′​k→′∗​(x→)​ψn​k→​(x→)​ei​q→⋅x→|2.|f_{i\rightarrow f}(\vec{q})|^{2}=|f_{n\vec{k}\rightarrow n^{\prime}\vec{k}^{\prime}}(\vec{q})|^{2}=\left|\int\text{d}^{3}x\,\psi_{n^{\prime}\vec{k}^{\prime}}^{*}(\vec{x})\psi_{n\vec{k}}(\vec{x})e^{i\vec{q}\cdot\vec{x}}\right|^{2}~. (76)

The Bloch state wavefunctions ψn​k→\psi_{n\vec{k}} are

ψn​k→​(x→)=1V​∑G→un​(k→+G→)​ei⁡(k→+G→)⋅x→,\displaystyle\psi_{n\vec{k}}(\vec{x})=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{V}}\sum_{\vec{G}}u_{n}(\vec{k}+\vec{G})e^{i(\vec{k}+\vec{G})\cdot\vec{x}}~, (77)

where the summation is over all reciprocal lattice vectors G→\vec{G}, VV is the volume of the crystal, and unu_{n} are normalized wavefunctions satisfying

∑G→|un​(k→+G→)|2=1.\sum_{\vec{G}}|u_{n}(\vec{k}+\vec{G})|^{2}=1~. (78)

Thus,

|fn​k→→n′​k→′​(q→)|2=|∫d3​x​1V​∑G→′un′∗​(k→′+G→′)​ei⁡(k→′+G→′)⋅x→​∑G→un​(k→+G→)​ei⁡(k→+G→)⋅x→​ei​q→⋅x→|2.\displaystyle|f_{n\vec{k}\rightarrow n^{\prime}\vec{k}^{\prime}}(\vec{q})|^{2}=\left|\int\text{d}^{3}x\,\frac{1}{V}\sum_{\vec{G}^{\prime}}u^{*}_{n^{\prime}}(\vec{k}^{\prime}+\vec{G}^{\prime})e^{i(\vec{k}^{\prime}+\vec{G}^{\prime})\cdot\vec{x}}\sum_{\vec{G}}u_{n}(\vec{k}+\vec{G})e^{i(\vec{k}+\vec{G})\cdot\vec{x}}e^{i\vec{q}\cdot\vec{x}}~\right|^{2}~. (79)

For crystal dimensions much larger than the atomic separation (we consider only large detectors where the interactions happen in the volume and surface effects are negligible) the discrete crystal momentum k→\vec{k} can be approximated by a continuous variable, thus

∫d3​x​ei​k→⋅x→=(2​π)3​δ3​(k→),\displaystyle\int\text{d}^{3}x~e^{i\vec{k}\cdot\vec{x}}=(2\pi)^{3}\delta^{3}(\vec{k})~, (80)

and the summation over states in Eq. (65) becomes

∑i,f=2∑n​n′∫BZV​d3​k(2​π)3V​d3​k′(2​π)3.\displaystyle\sum_{i,f}=2\sum_{nn^{\prime}}\int_{\rm BZ}\frac{V\text{d}^{3}k}{(2\pi)^{3}}\frac{V\text{d}^{3}k^{\prime}}{(2\pi)^{3}}~. (81)

1V​∑G→′un​(k→′+G→′)​ei⁡(k→′+G→′)⋅x→=1V​∑G→′un​(k→′+G→′+G→)​ei⁡(k→′+G→′+G→)⋅x→,\displaystyle\frac{1}{\sqrt{V}}\sum_{\vec{G}^{\prime}}u_{n}(\vec{k}^{\prime}+\vec{G}^{\prime})e^{i(\vec{k}^{\prime}+\vec{G}^{\prime})\cdot\vec{x}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{V}}\sum_{\vec{G}^{\prime}}u_{n}(\vec{k}^{\prime}+\vec{G}^{\prime}+\vec{G})e^{i(\vec{k}^{\prime}+\vec{G}^{\prime}+\vec{G})\cdot\vec{x}}~, (82)

Appendix D Expression for numerical calculations of the response function for general a, b and c constants

We use the computed electron form factors of Ref. [19] for Xe, Ge and Si target, but our analysis is general and our treatment is readily applicable to any given electron form factors that can be described by binned data with a power law dependency of qaq^{a} and ERbE_{\rm R}^{b}, where a,ba,b are integers, so that

|fi,f​(q±,ER)|2=q±a​ERb​|fdati,f​(ER,q±)|2.|f^{i,f}(q_{\pm},E_{\rm R})|^{2}=q_{\pm}^{a}E_{\rm R}^{b}|f^{i,f}_{\rm dat}(E_{\rm R},q_{\pm})|^{2}~. (89)

In the particular cases we consider in this paper, a=−3a=-3 and b=1b=1 for crystals (see Eq. (56)) and a=b=0a=b=0 for an atom (see Eq. (53)). Writing additionally |FDM​(q)|2=(α​me)2​c​q−2​c|F_{\rm DM}(q)|^{2}=(\alpha m_{e})^{2c}q^{-2c}, where either c=0c=0 or c=2c=2 are our two choices, the response function integral to be evaluated in Eq. (39) takes the functional form

d​ℛ±d​E′​(vmin,E′)\displaystyle\frac{d\mathcal{R}_{\pm}}{dE^{\prime}}(v_{\rm min},E^{\prime}) =\displaystyle= ϵ⁡(E′)4​μχ​e2​σE​(α​me)2​c​∑′i,f′​∫E′−σEEmaxd​ER​ERb−1​q±a+1−2​c​(vmin,ER+EB​i)\displaystyle\frac{\epsilon(E^{\prime})}{4\mu_{\chi e}^{2}\sigma_{\rm E}}(\alpha m_{e})^{2c}\sideset{}{{}^{\prime}}{\sum}_{i,f}\int_{E^{\prime}-\sigma_{\rm E}}^{E_{\rm max}}\text{d}E_{\rm R}\,E_{\rm R}^{b-1}~q^{a+1-2c}_{\pm}(v_{\rm min},E_{\rm R}+E_{{\rm B}i})~ (90)
×\displaystyle\times J±​(vmin,ER+EB​i)​|fdati,f​(ER,q±​(vmin,ER+EB​i))|2.\displaystyle J_{\pm}(v_{\rm min},E_{\rm R}+E_{{\rm B}i})|f^{i,f}_{\rm dat}(E_{\rm R},q_{\pm}(v_{\rm min},E_{\rm R}+E_{{\rm B}i}))|^{2}~.

Extracting the constant data value for the electron form factor in each bin and performing the remaining integral analytically, the expression we compute numerically is

d​ℛ±d​E′=ϵ⁡(E′)4​μχ​e2​σE​(α​me)2​c​∑′i,f′​∑Path⁡(r,s)Ia​b​c±,i​(vmin,E1(r​s),E2(r​s))​|fdati,f|r​s2,\displaystyle\frac{d\mathcal{R_{\pm}}}{dE^{\prime}}=\frac{\epsilon(E^{\prime})}{4\mu_{\chi e}^{2}\sigma_{\rm E}}(\alpha m_{e})^{2c}\sideset{}{{}^{\prime}}{\sum}_{i,f}\sum_{{\rm Path}(r,s)}I^{\pm,i}_{abc}(v_{\rm min},E_{1}^{(rs)},E_{2}^{(rs)})~|f^{i,f}_{\rm dat}|^{2}_{rs}~, (91)

where the summation is over all the (r,s)(r,s) partitions through which the path described by the function q⁡(vmin,ER)q(v_{\rm min},E_{\rm R}) passes, as indicated in Fig. 5. The analytically computed Ia​b​c±,i​(E1(r​s),E2(r​s))I^{\pm,i}_{abc}(E_{1}^{(rs)},E_{2}^{(rs)}) integrals are

Ia​b​c±,i​(vmin,E1(r​s),E2(r​s))=∫E1(r​s)E2(r​s)d​ERER1−b​q±a+1−2​c​(vmin,ER+EB​i)​J±​(vmin,ER+EB​i).\displaystyle I^{\pm,i}_{abc}(v_{\rm min},E_{1}^{(rs)},E_{2}^{(rs)})=\int_{E_{1}^{(rs)}}^{E_{2}^{(rs)}}\dfrac{\text{d}E_{\rm R}}{E_{\rm R}^{1-b}}\,q^{a+1-2c}_{\pm}(v_{\rm min},E_{\rm R}+E_{{\rm B}i})J_{\pm}(v_{\rm min},E_{\rm R}+E_{{\rm B}i})~. (92)

Here, E1(r​s)E_{1}^{(rs)} and E2(r​s)E_{2}^{(rs)} are the boundaries of the shaded area in the partition (r​s)(rs) shown in Fig. 5. Since the partitions are small, we use the approximation ER≈(E1(r​s)+E2(r​s))/2E_{\rm R}\approx(E_{1}^{(rs)}+E_{2}^{(rs)})/2 and take ERb−1E_{\rm R}^{b-1} outside the integral, so Eq. (92) becomes

Ia​b​c±,i​(vmin,E1(r​s),E2(r​s))≃2​∫E1(r​s)E2(r​s)d​ER​q±a+1−2​c​(vmin,ER+EB​i)​J±​(vmin,ER+EB​i)(E1(r​s)+E2(r​s))1−b.I^{\pm,i}_{abc}(v_{\rm min},E_{1}^{(rs)},E_{2}^{(rs)})\simeq 2\int_{E_{1}^{(rs)}}^{E_{2}^{(rs)}}\text{d}E_{\rm R}\,\frac{q^{a+1-2c}_{\pm}(v_{\rm min},E_{\rm R}+E_{{\rm B}i})\,J_{\pm}(v_{\rm min},E_{\rm R}+E_{{\rm B}i})}{\left(E_{1}^{(rs)}+E_{2}^{(rs)}\right)^{1-b}}~. for a−2​c≠−3a-2c\neq-3,

×[(1±1−2​(ER+EB​i)m​vmin2)a−2​c+3]|E1(r​s)E2(r​s).\displaystyle\times\left.\left[\left(1\pm\sqrt{1-\dfrac{2(E_{\rm R}+E_{{\rm B}i})}{mv_{\rm min}^{2}}}\right)^{a-2c+3}\right]\right|_{E_{1}^{(rs)}}^{E_{2}^{(rs)}}~.

Both of them are always positive.

Appendix E Alternative derivation of the response function for DM scattering off electrons

The response function d​ℛ/d​E′\text{d}\mathcal{R}/\text{d}E^{\prime} can be derived using the relation in Eq. (12)

d​ℛd​E′​(vmin,E′)≡∂∂vmin​[d​ℋd​E′​(vmin,E′)],\frac{\text{d}\mathcal{R}}{\text{d}E^{\prime}}(v_{\rm min},E^{\prime})\equiv\frac{\partial}{\partial v_{\rm min}}\left[\frac{\text{d}\mathcal{H}}{\text{d}E^{\prime}}(v_{\rm min},E^{\prime})\right]\,, (96)

from the response function d​ℋ​(vmin,E′)/d​E′{\text{d}\mathcal{H}}(v_{\rm min},E^{\prime})/{\text{d}E^{\prime}} to the speed distribution, when we write the rate as in Eq. (9), namely

d​Rd​E′=σ¯e​ρm​∫0∞d​v​F⁡(v,t)v​d​ℋd​E′​(v,E′).\frac{\text{d}R}{\text{d}E^{\prime}}=\frac{\overline{\sigma}_{e}\rho}{m}\int_{0}^{\infty}{\rm d}v~\frac{F(v,t)}{v}\frac{{\rm d}\mathcal{H}}{{\rm d}E^{\prime}}(v,E^{\prime})\,. (97)

This procedure allows us to make contact with the formulation used for DM scattering off nuclei, in particular for inelastic scattering, as explained in App F.

Starting from Eq. (64) and using Eq. (66) and Eq. (67) we get

d​Rd​ER=∑′i,f′​ρ​σ¯e4​π​μχ​e2​m​ER​∫d3​v​fχ​(v→)​∫d3​qq​v​δ​(cos⁡θq​v−vminv)​|FDM​(q)|2​|fi,f​(q,ER)|2,\displaystyle\dfrac{\text{d}R}{\text{d}E_{\rm R}}=\sideset{}{{}^{\prime}}{\sum}_{i,f}\frac{\rho~\overline{\sigma}_{e}}{4\pi\mu^{2}_{\chi e}mE_{\rm R}}\int\text{d}^{3}vf_{\chi}(\vec{v})\int\frac{\text{d}^{3}q}{qv}\delta(\cos\theta_{qv}-\frac{v_{\rm min}}{v})|F_{\rm DM}(q)|^{2}|f^{i,f}(q,E_{\rm R})|^{2}, (98)

or after further simplification

d​Rd​ER=∑′i,f′​ρm​σ¯e2​μχ​e2​ER​∫v~d​v​F⁡(v)v​∫q−​(v,Ee)q+​(v,Ee)d​q​q​|FDM​(q)|2​|fi,f​(q,ER)|2,\displaystyle\dfrac{\text{d}R}{\text{d}E_{\rm R}}=\sideset{}{{}^{\prime}}{\sum}_{i,f}\frac{\rho}{m}\frac{\overline{\sigma}_{e}}{2\mu^{2}_{\chi e}E_{\rm R}}\int_{\tilde{v}}\text{d}v\,\frac{F(v)}{v}\int_{q_{-}(v,E_{e})}^{q_{+}(v,E_{e})}\text{d}q\,q~|F_{\rm DM}(q)|^{2}~|f^{i,f}(q,E_{\rm R})|^{2}~, (99)

where v~=2​Ee/m\tilde{v}=\sqrt{2E_{e}/m} and the functions q±​(v,Ee)q_{\pm}(v,E_{e}) are given in Eq. (25). Integrating now on ERE_{\rm R} to obtain the observable differential rate d​R/d​E′{\text{d}R}/{\text{d}E^{\prime}} we identify d​ℋ​(E′,v)/d​E′{\text{d}\mathcal{H}}(E^{\prime},v)/{\text{d}E^{\prime}} as

d​ℋd​E′​(v,E′)≡{ϵ⁡(E′)2​μχ​e2​∫d​ERER​G​(E′,ER)​∑′i,f′​∫q−​(v,Ee)q+​(v,Ee)d​q​q​|FDM​(q)|2​|fi,f​(q,ER)|2 if v⩾v~,0 if v<v~.\displaystyle\dfrac{\text{d}\mathcal{H}}{\text{d}E^{\prime}}(v,E^{\prime})\equiv\begin{cases}\hfill\frac{\epsilon(E^{\prime})}{2\mu^{2}_{\chi e}}\int\frac{\text{d}E_{\rm R}}{E_{\rm R}}G(E^{\prime},E_{\rm R})\sideset{}{{}^{\prime}}{\sum}_{i,f}\int_{q_{-}(v,E_{e})}^{q_{+}(v,E_{e})}\text{d}q\,q|F_{\rm DM}(q)|^{2}|f^{i,f}(q,E_{\rm R})|^{2}\hfill&\text{ if $v\geqslant\tilde{v}$,}\\ &\\ \hfill 0\hfill&\text{ if $v<\tilde{v}$.}\\ \end{cases} (100)

Notice that this expression depends on the speed vv only though the limits of the integration in qq. Taking the partial derivative of this expression with respect to vv, and recalling we defined in Eq. (34) ∂q±​(v,Ee)/∂v=J±​(v,Ee){\partial q_{\pm}(v,E_{e})}/{\partial v}=J_{\pm}(v,E_{e}), we recover Eqs. (38) and (39).

Appendix F Comparison with the formalism for DM scattering off nuclei

In DM-electron scattering, with kinematics described by Eq. (23), two of the three variables - momentum transfer qq, detectable energy ERE_{\rm R}, and vminv_{\rm min} - are independent. In the halo-dependent usual formalism, vminv_{\rm min} is taken to be a function of the other two. In the halo-independent formalism, we choose instead ERE_{\rm R} and vminv_{\rm min} as independent variables, and thus we change an integration in qq to obtain the rate into an integration in vminv_{\rm min}.

In the DM scattering off nuclei (of mass mNm_{N}) the kinematics sets ER=q2/2​mNE_{\rm R}=q^{2}/2m_{N}, and only one of the two variables ERE_{\rm R} and vminv_{\rm min} is independent. In the halo-independent method we chose vminv_{\rm min} to be the independent variable and thus change an integration in ERE_{\rm R} to get the predicted event rate into an integration in vminv_{\rm min}.

In spite of these differences in the kinematics of DM-electron scattering and DM-nucleus scattering, we can identify a similarity in the equations we get in qq in DM scattering off electrons and in ERE_{\rm R} in the inelastic endothermic DM scattering off nuclei. In this latter case, the DM particles scatter to a new state of mass m′=m+δm^{\prime}=m+\delta, where |δ|≪m|\delta|\ll m, and δ>0\delta>0 (<0<0) describes endothermic (exothermic) scattering. In this case (see e.g. Refs. [64, 82, 83]), in the limit μχ​N​|δ|/m2≪1\mu_{\chi N}|\delta|/m^{2}\ll 1, vmin​(ER)v_{\rm min}(E_{\rm R}) is

vmin​(ER)=12​mN​ER​|mN​ERμχ​N+δ|,v_{\rm min}(E_{\rm R})=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2m_{N}E_{\rm R}}}\left|\frac{m_{N}E_{\rm R}}{\mu_{\chi N}}+\delta\right|\,, (101)

which reduces to the typical equation for elastic scattering when δ=0\delta=0. Thus, the range of possible recoil energies that can be imparted to a target nucleus by a DM particle traveling at speed vv in Earth’s frame is [ER−​(v),ER+​(v)][E_{\rm R}^{-}(v),E_{\rm R}^{+}(v)], where

ER±​(v)=μχ​N2​v22​mN​(1±1−2​δμχ​N​v2)2.E_{\rm R}^{\pm}(v)=\frac{\mu_{\chi N}^{2}v^{2}}{2m_{N}}\left(1\pm\sqrt{1-\frac{2\delta}{\mu_{\chi N}~v^{2}}}\right)^{2}\,. (102)

For endothermic scattering the minimum possible value of vv is vδN=2​δ/μχ​N>0v_{\delta}^{N}=\sqrt{2\delta/\mu_{\chi N}}>0, which depends on the nuclide type through the reduced mass μχ​N\mu_{\chi N} (for exothermic and elastic scattering the minimum is instead vδ=0v_{\delta}=0). Notice the similarity of the definition of ER±​(v)E_{\rm R}^{\pm}(v) in Eq. (102) with the definition of q±​(v,Ee)q_{\pm}(v,E_{e}) in Eq. (25). In Eq. (99), for a fixed speed vv the integration in qq is between q−q_{-} and q+q_{+}, and similarly here the integration for fixed speed is between ER−E_{\rm R}^{-} and ER+E_{\rm R}^{+}. The differential rate as a function of the detected energy E′E^{\prime} for DM scattering off a nuclide NN is (see Eq. (4), Eq. (5), Eq. (8) and Eq. (9))

d​RNd​E′=ϵ⁡(E′)​∫0∞d​ER​GN​(E′,ER)​d​RNd​ER.\frac{\text{d}R_{N}}{\text{d}E^{\prime}}=\epsilon(E^{\prime})\int_{0}^{\infty}\text{d}E_{\rm R}\,G_{N}(E^{\prime},E_{\rm R})\,\frac{\text{d}R_{N}}{\text{d}E_{\rm R}}~. (103)

Thus, summing over all nuclides in the target the total rate can be written in the form

d​Rd​E′=σref​ρm​∫v⩾vδd3​v​fχ​(v→,t)v​d​ℋd​E′​(v→,E′),\frac{\text{d}R}{\text{d}E^{\prime}}=\frac{\sigma_{\text{ref}}\rho}{m}\int_{v\geqslant v_{\delta}}\text{d}^{3}v\,\frac{f_{\chi}(\vec{v},t)}{v}\,\frac{\text{d}\mathcal{H}}{\text{d}E^{\prime}}(\vec{v},E^{\prime})\,, (104)

where the response function d​ℋ/d​E′=∑Nd​ℋN/d​E′\text{d}\mathcal{H}/{\text{d}E^{\prime}}=\sum_{N}\text{d}\mathcal{H}_{N}/{\text{d}E^{\prime}} (Eq. (10)) is [64, 82, 83]

d​ℋd​E′​(v→,E′)≡{∑NNN​∫ER−ER+d​ER​ϵ​(E′,ER)​GN​(ER,E′)​v2σref​d​σNd​ER​(ER,v→) if v⩾vδ,0 if v<vδ.\frac{\text{d}\mathcal{H}}{\text{d}E^{\prime}}(\vec{v},E^{\prime})\equiv\begin{cases}\hfill\sum_{N}N_{N}\int_{E_{\rm R}^{-}}^{E_{\rm R}^{+}}\,\text{d}E_{\rm R}\,\epsilon(E^{\prime},E_{\rm R})\,G_{N}(E_{\rm R},E^{\prime})\,\frac{v^{2}}{\sigma_{\text{ref}}}\,\frac{\text{d}\sigma_{N}}{\text{d}E_{\rm R}}(E_{\rm R},\vec{v})\hfill&\text{ if $v\geqslant v_{\delta}$,}\\ \hfill 0\hfill&\text{ if $v<v_{\delta}$.}\end{cases} (105)

Here, NNN_{N} is the number of nuclei per unit mass of the detector, σN\sigma_{N} is the DM-nucleus scattering cross section and vδv_{\delta} is the smallest of the speed threshold values vδNv_{\delta}^{N} for all nuclides in the target. Notice the formal similarity between Eq. (105) and Eq. (100). Similarly to the response function in Eq. (100), the response function for nuclear scattering in Eq. (105) depends only on the speed vv, instead of the velocity vector v→\vec{v} if the scattering does not depend on the direction of the incoming DM particle.

As for DM scattering off electrons, also for inelastic endothermic scattering off nuclei for which vδ≠0v_{\delta}\not=0 (these are Eq. (11) to Eq. (15) applied to this type of DM)

d​Rd​E′=−∫vδ∞dv∂η~​(v,t)∂vd​ℋd​E′(v,E′),\frac{\text{d}R}{\text{d}E^{\prime}}=-\int_{v_{\delta}}^{\infty}\text{d}v\,\frac{\partial\tilde{\eta}(v,t)}{\partial v}\,\frac{\text{d}\mathcal{H}}{\text{d}E^{\prime}}(v,E^{\prime})\,, (106)

and, using that η~​(∞,t)=0\tilde{\eta}(\infty,t)=0 and d​ℋ/d​E′​(E′,vδ)=0\text{d}\mathcal{H}/\text{d}E^{\prime}(E^{\prime},v_{\delta})=0, integrating Eq. (106) by parts results in

d​Rd​E′=∫vδ∞d​vmin​η~​(vmin,t)​d​ℛd​E′​(vmin,E′),\frac{\text{d}R}{\text{d}E^{\prime}}=\int_{v_{\delta}}^{\infty}\text{d}v_{\rm min}\tilde{\eta}(v_{\rm min},t)\,\frac{\text{d}\mathcal{R}}{\text{d}E^{\prime}}(v_{\rm min},E^{\prime})\,, (107)

where the differential response function d​ℛ/d​E′\text{d}\mathcal{R}/\text{d}E^{\prime} is

d​ℛd​E′​(vmin,E′)≡∂∂vmin​[d​ℋd​E′​(vmin,E′)].\frac{\text{d}\mathcal{R}}{\text{d}E^{\prime}}(v_{\rm min},E^{\prime})\equiv\frac{\partial}{\partial v_{\rm min}}\left[\frac{\text{d}\mathcal{H}}{\text{d}E^{\prime}}(v_{\rm min},E^{\prime})\right]\,. (108)

As for DM scattering off electrons, here if vδv_{\delta} is in the observable range of an experiment, the response function d​ℛ​d​E′{\text{d}\mathcal{R}}{\text{d}E^{\prime}} depends on a Jacobian factor ∂ER±/∂ER\partial{E_{\rm R}}^{\pm}/\partial E_{\rm R} which is singular at v=vδv=v_{\delta}.

Instructions for reporting errors

We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the methods listed below:

  • Click the "Report Issue" () button, located in the page header.

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.

Our team has already identified the following issues. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for all.
